question: A department switches all fifty of its staff to a redesigned, Claude-assisted case-handling process on the same Monday morning, with no trial group kept back. What is the greatest risk?
options: A) The department's usage may rise sharply in the first week as fifty people start using Claude.
B) Some staff will need considerably longer than others to become comfortable with the new way of working.
C) Any flaw hits every case at once, and there is no unchanged group to compare results against.
D) Training all fifty staff in one week will strain the two people who designed the new process.
correct_answers: C) Any flaw hits every case at once, and there is no unchanged group to compare results against.
explanations: A jump in usage is a predictable consequence of fifty people starting at once and can be planned for. It affects cost and capacity, not the soundness of the redesigned process.
Uneven adoption is expected in any change and is managed with support and coaching. It slows the benefit rather than exposing the department to a failure it cannot see.

Correct. A full switch removes both safeguards at once: every case is exposed to a design that has never run live, and with no group still on the old process there is nothing to compare against, so the team cannot even tell whether results have got worse.
Straining the two designers is a real resourcing problem during the first week. It is a delivery pressure rather than the reason a simultaneous switch is dangerous.
